title: Hazel and the Cellar
premise: Freya Amberdale takes a teaching post in the village of Hollowmere, where a class of children vanished into the school cellar in 1974 and no one will say how. When the church bell—melted down decades ago—begins to ring, Freya and her students are pulled into the cellar's folded time, where the missing children still wait, hungry for someone to take their place. To escape, Freya must return what was stolen in 1974: not an object, but a name, erased from every record to seal the bargain that saved the village. In the end, Freya gives the bell its true toll, restores the forgotten child's name at terrible personal cost, and leads her found family out—though one of them chooses to stay behind so the door can close.
about_author: Odile Fairweather is a former village schoolteacher who spent eleven years collecting oral histories from communities that preferred to be forgotten. She writes horror from a converted chapel on the Yorkshire moors, where she keeps meticulous count of her doors.

chapters.title: The Position
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She arrives in Hollowmere for the autumn term, charmed by the school but unsettled by the cellar door painted shut beneath the stairwell. The headmaster warns her never to count the children aloud. Emotional beat: hopeful new beginnings shadowed by small wrongness.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Her register lists twenty-six pupils; only twenty-five ever attend. The absent name is smudged beyond reading. A student, Idris, flinches when she asks about it. Emotional beat: quiet dread taking root in routine.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Establishing her rituals: lamps lit before dusk, doors counted twice nightly. The caretaker, Mrs. Pell, approves grimly, saying the last teacher who stopped counting 'went down.' Emotional beat: comfort of ritual as armor.

chapters.title: The Bell That Isn't
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Walking home past the empty belfry, Idris hears a single toll though the bell was melted in 1911. The sound leaves frost on his collar in September. Emotional beat: childhood certainty cracking.

chapters.title: Local History Week
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Preparing lessons, she finds the 1911 parish record confirming the bell's melting—and a 1974 school photo with one child's face scratched out. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell's Warning
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell's POV. The old caretaker remembers 1974 firsthand: the class went down for a fire drill and only some came up. The village paid a price to close the cellar. She begs Freya to resign. Emotional beat: guilt passed down like inheritance.

chapters.title: Second Toll
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The bell rings twice during assembly; every child freezes mid-word. Frost blooms across the windows spelling half a word. Emotional beat: collective held breath.

chapters.title: What Idris Saw
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He confesses he's been hearing the bell for weeks and dreaming of a classroom below the cellar with twenty-six desks. Emotional beat: fear shared becomes bearable—the first bond of found family.

chapters.title: The Painted Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The paint on the cellar door has begun to blister and peel from the inside. Beneath it, older paint reads a rule: WHAT GOES DOWN ANSWERS WHEN CALLED. Emotional beat: safety revealed as postponement.

chapters.title: Archives at the Vicarage
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The vicar shows her records; the 1974 register page is razored out. He mentions a child whose name was 'unwritten' by unanimous vote. Emotional beat: institutional complicity, the horror of polite people.

chapters.title: Third Toll
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, braided. Three tolls; the school's electricity dies; the children hold hands in the dark while Freya counts them by touch—twenty-five, always twenty-five. Emotional beat: terror transformed into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Down the Stairwell
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Chasing Idris, who sleepwalks toward the cellar, Freya breaks the painted seal. The stairs descend farther than the building should allow. Emotional beat: point of no return, chosen for love.

chapters.title: The Under-Classroom
chapters.summary: Freya and Idris's POV. They find the mirrored classroom: twenty-six desks, chalk dust, a lesson still in progress on the board dated October 1974. Children watch from the gloom. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition—they've been expected.

chapters.title: The Twenty-Sixth Desk
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. One desk bears a nameplate worn blank. The ghost-children explain without words: their classmate was given to the cellar, and the village unwrote her name to make it legal. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who was made unrememberable.

chapters.title: Return Above
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They climb back; hours have passed in minutes. But frost now follows Freya, and Idris hums a tune none of them taught him. Emotional beat: escape that isn't escape.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers Wrongly
chapters.summary: Multiple villagers' POVs. Freya interviews households; each describes the missing child differently or not at all, memories sliding off like rain. Emotional beat: frustration and dawning horror at engineered forgetting.

chapters.title: Pell Breaks
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell's POV. Confronted, the caretaker confesses: the village traded the girl—Edith? Edna?—to end the hauntings after the bell was melted. The name was struck so the debt couldn't be traced. Emotional beat: confession as partial absolution, mostly shame.

chapters.title: Fourth Toll
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Four tolls; the frost word completes itself: RETURN. The cellar has begun calling names, starting with the oldest villagers. Mr. Halloway next door doesn't answer his door anymore. Emotional beat: deadline made audible.

chapters.title: Researching Edith
chapters.summary: Freya and Idris's POV. Digging through county records, they recover fragments: E-d-i-t-h, born 1963, liked marbles. Each recovered letter makes the bell louder. Emotional beat: hope with a rising cost.

chapters.title: The Marbles
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. In the school loft, Idris finds a tin of marbles labeled in a child's hand: EDITH'S — DO NOT TAKE. Taking one, he hears her voice clearly for the first time. Emotional beat: tender contact across fifty years.

chapters.title: The Bargain's Terms
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In dreams, the cellar explains: return what was taken—a life freely offered must be freely returned, or a name restored and honored. Half-measures feed it. Emotional beat: rules understood too late.

chapters.title: Vicar's Dilemma
chapters.summary: The vicar's POV. Torn between protecting his flock and repenting the parish's sin, he burns his copy of the 1974 agreement—and the fire burns green. Emotional beat: cowardice meeting consequence.

chapters.title: Fifth Toll
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Five tolls; the school's upper floors grow cold and wrong, corridors looping. Parents begin keeping children home. Freya refuses to evacuate: leaving means the cellar takes the whole village. Emotional beat: leadership under siege.

chapters.title: A Name Restored
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya writes EDITH AMBERDALE—no; research reveals Edith's surname matches her own family line. The taken child was kin. The call wasn't random. Emotional beat: personal stake detonated.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Among her late grandmother's effects, Freya finds letters proving her grandmother was the teacher of 1974—who chose Edith, her own niece, to save the rest. Emotional beat: inherited guilt, the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Sixth Toll
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Six tolls; Idris begins fading, frost in his lungs, the cellar claiming him as collateral since he touched Edith's marbles. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened by love.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. A midnight meeting: some vote to offer Idris and flee; Mrs. Pell stands and says 'Never again.' The room splits. Emotional beat: community fracturing along the same fault line as 1974.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya prepares the rite: the marbles, the restored name written in bell-metal ink, her grandmother's confession read aloud. She quietly plans to stay herself as payment. Emotional beat: calm resolve masking sacrifice.

chapters.title: Seventh Toll
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Seven tolls; the cellar door opens on its own; the under-classroom rises into the school like water filling a hull. Desks appear between real ones. Emotional beat: boundary collapse, full dread.

chapters.title: Descent, Second Time
chapters.summary: Freya, Idris, Mrs. Pell's POV. The three go down together, armed with truth instead of paint and locks. The ghost-children part before them. Emotional beat: courage as communal act.

chapters.title: Edith Found
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the bottom sits Edith, unchanged since 1974, holding attendance marks for every day. She asks only: 'Does anyone remember me now?' Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: The Reading of Names
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. In the under-classroom, Freya reads all twenty-six names aloud, ending with Edith's, restored. With each name, a ghost-child brightens. Emotional beat: memory as resurrection.

chapters.title: The Bell Demands
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The bell tolls eight times and demands balance: a life for a life. Freya steps forward—but Edith refuses her, having waited fifty years precisely so no one else would pay. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused, grace offered.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell's POV. The caretaker reveals she was meant to be the 1974 offering and has owed the cellar her whole life. She offers herself freely—the debt finally honestly paid. Emotional beat: redemption through volition.

chapters.title: The Ninth Toll
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mrs. Pell crosses over; the bell rings nine times and falls silent forever. The under-classroom dissolves into warm dust. Edith, freed, fades smiling, her marbles left in Idris's hands. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Climbing Out
chapters.summary: Freya and Idris's POV. They ascend stairs that are suddenly ordinary. Dawn light. The school smells of chalk and nothing else. Emotional beat: exhaustion, disbelief, survival.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The village wakes remembering everything at once—weeping, laying flowers, carving Edith's name into the war memorial wall. The vicar resigns. Emotional beat: communal reckoning, painful and cleansing.

chapters.title: The New Register
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya rewrites the register with twenty-six names and teaches the children the counting ritual—not from fear now, but remembrance. Idris keeps Edith's marbles on his desk. Emotional beat: ritual transfigured into love.

chapters.title: Doors Counted, Lights Kept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, closing. Spring term. Freya counts her doors each night and finds the number good. Sometimes, faintly, a bell note sounds—warm now, like thanks. She teaches on. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept as devotion rather than dread.
